quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The height from the road to a bridge or overpass.
The maximum legal height for vehicles in this state.
The maximum width for vehicles on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The height from the road to a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This is a low clearance warning sign. It tells you the distance from the road to the bottom of a bridge or overpass. In this example, it is 12 feet, 6 inches.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
When the yellow line on your side is broken.
When the yellow line on the opposite side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line in the center means traffic on the broken line side may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: As daylight fades, what should you use so others can see you?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams when daylight starts to fade. Use high beams only in open areas with no other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Fight the feeling.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: Stop at the next rest area or service station. Take a nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Do not rely on caffeine pills or drinks—they are not a safe substitute for rest.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes in your direction. Many vehicles pass you on the right. The driver behind wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane to avoid blocking traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.
Move to the right lane when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for passing and turning left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: What does this yellow road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of curves.
Traffic increases ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings tell you the road is slippery when wet. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Stay farther back than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than normal.
questions.explanation: Keep 3 to 4 seconds behind a motorcycle. They stop quickly and you need extra distance in case they fall. The risk is greatest on wet roads, gravel, and metal surfaces.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlight beam.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead.
Keep your instrument lights bright to be visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlight beam.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night because you cannot see as far ahead. Always be able to stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid fast turns and stops.
Test your tire traction going uphill.
Look closer to your vehicle instead of ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire traction. Drive slower and avoid quick turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, what speed should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Continue. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for them to cross.
Pull right and go around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for them to cross.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding.

questions.question: What can a bad suspension cause?

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps control your vehicle and smooth out bumps. If your car bounces a lot or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: What message appears on this yellow pennant-shaped sign?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns permitted.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped yellow signs mark a no passing zone.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is injured in a collision?

options.text: Do not move them unless absolutely necessary.
Move them where they want to go.
Tell them they are fine and do not need medical help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless there is immediate danger like fire. Keep them sitting or lying down until medical help arrives.

questions.question: You park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should your wheels point?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Right, toward the side of the road.
Left, toward the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels so the vehicle rolls away from traffic if the brakes fail, whether parking uphill or downhill on a road without a curb.

questions.question: A vehicle cuts in front of you suddenly. What is the first thing you should do?

options.text: Honk and brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas.
Swerve to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle merges too close, release the gas pedal. This creates space without hard braking or swerving into another lane.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the driver signals you to return.
After signaling for three seconds.
When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This means you have enough distance.

questions.question: Can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: Yes, if you entered on a green light.
Yes, during rush hour.
No, under no circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Never block an intersection. Even with a green light, only enter if you can clear the intersection before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: When should your wheels not point straight ahead?

options.text: While waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on a level roadside with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: While waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight so you do not veer into traffic if hit from behind. On hills, angle wheels so the vehicle will not roll into traffic if brakes fail.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer distances to stop and cause more severe crashes.

questions.question: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue moving to clear the intersection as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Motorcycles and scooters are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down while driving.
Check all around you constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check all around you constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can hide in your blind spots or be missed because they are small. Always look carefully for motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds.

questions.question: Where should a driver look while driving?

options.text: Straight ahead at the road in front of the car.
Only at the middle of the road.
To the sides, ahead, and behind the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the sides, ahead, and behind the car.
questions.explanation: Look to the sides, ahead, and behind your car. Good drivers know what is happening all around their vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Traffic is merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to allow traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: When should you yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave at you first.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Always stop at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. You may only proceed when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use the side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all blind spots. Before changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check these areas.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep scanning the road for possible dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep scanning the road for possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means constantly looking ahead and around for hazards. Do not stare only at the road directly in front of your car.

questions.question: When passing a large truck, what should you do?

options.text: Move back to your lane quickly and slow down.
Give the truck plenty of space before moving back.
Move back to your lane whenever you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the truck plenty of space before moving back.
questions.explanation: Do not return to your lane too quickly after passing a truck. Wait until you see the entire front of the truck in your mirror. Trucks need about twice as long to stop as regular cars.

questions.question: When is a highway most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain first begins.
After one to two hours of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first begins.
questions.explanation: The road is most slippery when rain first starts. Oil and dirt on the pavement mix with water to create a slick surface.

questions.question: How much lane space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The same full width as other vehicles.
The width of the sidewalk.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the full width of a lane, just like other vehicles.

questions.question: How can you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out the back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror frequently to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: Before starting the car, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, buckle your belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means do not cross. A broken yellow line means you may cross only if it is safe.

questions.question: How do you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Merge into a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a different lane.
questions.explanation: If possible, move to another lane to create a gap for entering vehicles. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to let them merge safely.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Assume the child has full control of the bike.
Be ready for anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything.
questions.explanation: Children on bikes are unpredictable. They often make sudden changes in direction. Remember that children and bikes are small and hard to see.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right for construction.
The road ahead turns sharply at an extreme angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to an abrupt change in road direction. Slow down and be ready for the sharp turn.

questions.question: One solid yellow line and one broken yellow line mark the center. If the broken line is on your side, you can:

options.text: Not pass other vehicles.
Pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming.
Only make right turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you are in a passing zone and may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: As a driver, you should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Be ready to yield if it can prevent a collision.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended if you drive with what level of alcohol?

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any alcohol in their system. Any amount of alcohol will result in a suspended license for two years and other penalties.
